The Problem Isn't the Price It's the Retroactive Restrictions. They Changed the Rules After the Work Is Done

I have been a loyal Canva Pro customer for years. My biggest thumbs-down pet peeve is that Canva now retroactively locks assets behind new licensing tiers. Even when those assets were included in Pro when I created my designs, Canva later moved them to a higher tier and restricted access to my existing projects. As a result, I can no longer download some of my older projects without watermarks, even though I had full access to those stock images and graphics when I created them and still maintain a Canva Pro subscription. Canva moved assets from Pro to Business and, in doing so, effectively locked customers out of work they had already created. This has affected numerous projects in my account.

New content may require new subscriptions. What feels unfair is retroactively restricting assets in existing projects. If I created a design while paying for an active Pro subscription and the asset was included in Pro at the time, Canva should allow me to download that project forever.

Software companies view access as an ongoing rental. Customers view completed creative work as paid for, settled, and their own. Those expectations are now colliding. Canva built its success on trust and simplicity. I wish they would not undermine that trust by changing the rules on work their customers have already created.

Pay. Smooth sailing from there.. Short version: 
Definitely opt for the subscription if you're serious and can afford it. 

Long version: 
 Once you sign in (or log back in, since it logs you out after big updates and stuff) and get a subscription, you can easily make any design you can think of. In fact, you shouldn't go into the app without knowing for sure what you're going to do, otherwise, the possibilities will overwhelm you! 
 I'm only giving it four stars because the free app is practically just to convince you to start a subscription and not to be functional in its own right. Two thirds or possibly three fourths of all clip art, pictures, and videos are behind the paywall, as well as lots of good fonts and most of your "most-needed" features (brand kit, background removal, and almost all of the other image editing tools). Not that most other current apps aren't also like this, it's just that there isn't much point in any productivity app that limits productivity like this.

💀 0/5 stars (and a strongly worded letter to the Geneva Convention). Let me set the scene. I’m an *expert*. I’ve bent Photoshop to my will. I’ve coded UIs in my sleep. I once made a PowerPoint presentation that didn't crash. And yet, Canva this cheerful, pastel-colored insult to human intelligence has reduced me to a sobbing pile of incompetence.

The free version is basically a psychological experiment. Want to remove a background? *Subscribe.* Want to export without a watermark the size of a small car? *Subscribe.* Want to use a font that doesn't look like it was designed for a toddler's birthday party? *Subscribe, you peasant.* It’s not a design tool it’s a ransom note. "Nice design you've got there. Shame if something… *premium-only* happened to it."

But fine. I cave. I pay. I subscribe. I unlock the golden gates of Canva Pro.

And what do I find? **More chaos, now with glitter.**

Because apparently, "common sense" was part of the free tier they removed. Even as a paying customer, the app still behaves like a caffeinated squirrel with a keyboard. I try to resize an image? Suddenly my text is inside the moon, and the background has left for a pack of smokes. I click "undo"? My design time-travels to 2003 and applies neon green drop shadows. The alignment guides snap to *vibes*, not to anything rational.

The paid features? Let's talk about them. AI background remover works… when it feels like it. Sometimes it removes the background. Sometimes it removes the subject's head. Sometimes it just removes your will to live. And the "magic resize" feature? Oh, it resizes alright into a cursed 4:3 aspect ratio that crops out your logo and doubles the font size on your legal disclaimer. *Magic.*

Don't even get me started on performance. The app lags harder on a flagship phone than my brain trying to understand why a *rotate handle* needs to buffer for ten seconds. Premium subscription, premium lag. You love to see it.

So here's the truth, served with a heavy dose of sarcasm and a garnish of despair:

**Canva is equally useless whether you pay or not.** The free version taunts you. The paid version betrays you. Both assume you have the patience of a saint and the common sense of a goldfish. As an expert, you'll feel like you're piloting a spaceship made of wet cardboard. As a beginner, you'll cry. As a paying customer, you'll cry *faster*.

Highly recommended… if you're into self-flagellation and bad design decisions. Otherwise, just use MS Paint. At least it won't ask you for $12.99 a month to crop a circle.
